$comment: Per-scenario regression thresholds for the CI smoke gate, DERIVED FROM MEASUREMENT
rather than chosen. Re-derive them with scripts/measure-gate-noise.mjs if the
profile, the runner image, or the scenario set changes; do not hand-tune them.
Method: 8 consecutive TypeScript Benchmarks runs on ubuntu-latest (2026-08-16/17,
runs 31966981572 .. 32002271589) over commits that did not touch the request path,
compared against the per-row median of those same 8 runs. Any deviation there is
the runner, not the code.
What the data showed, and it is not noise around a mean: five runs landed within
1.4% of the median and three landed 39-43% below it. GitHub's shared pool has at
least two performance classes. The tell is that `compute` is UNAFFECTED on those
same three runs (99-109% throughout) while every I/O-bound scenario collapses --
a slower per-request path, not a slower CPU.
Normalising against another framework in the same run does not rescue it: on the
worst run Neutron drops 43% while Astro drops 17%, because the two do not have
the same sensitivity to per-request cost. So there is no arithmetic that recovers
sensitivity here -- the I/O-bound scenarios simply cannot see anything under ~2x
on this infrastructure, and pretending otherwise produces a gate that cries wolf.
Hence: `compute` gates tightly because it demonstrably can, everything else gates
at catastrophe level. A 10x regression is a 90% drop and is caught everywhere.
Worst observed deviation vs this baseline: 42.8% rps drop, 33.3% p95 increase.

compute.$why: CPU-bound and provably insensitive to the runner class: 99-109% of median across all 8 runs, including the three that lost 40% everywhere else. Worst observed drop 1.0%, so 25% is a 25x margin. This is the only scenario here that can catch a sub-2x regression.
